question.prompt: Let \(g(x)\) be a polynomial with leading coefficient \(1,\) whose three roots are the reciprocals of the three roots of \(f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c,\) where \(1\lt a\lt b\lt c.\) What is \(g(1)\) in terms of \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c?\)

solutions.title: Reverse the coefficients
solutions.explanation:
Replacing \(x\) by \(1/x\) turns nonzero roots into their reciprocals. Multiplying by \(x^3\) then clears the denominators.

Since \(c>0\), we have \(f(0)\ne0\), so all three roots of \(f\) are nonzero. Form the polynomial
\[
H(x)=x^3f(1/x)=1+ax+bx^2+cx^3.
\]
For any root \(r\) of \(f\),
\[
H(1/r)=\frac{f(r)}{r^3}=0.
\]
Thus \(H\) has the reciprocal roots, counted with multiplicity. Its leading coefficient is \(c\), so dividing by \(c\) produces the monic polynomial with those roots:
\[
g(x)=\frac{cx^3+bx^2+ax+1}{c}.
\]
Evaluating at \(x=1\), we obtain
\[
g(1)=\boxed{\frac{1+a+b+c}{c}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Compare the root products
solutions.explanation:
Because we need only \(g(1)\), its factored form lets us relate the answer directly to \(f(1)\) and the product of the original roots.

Let \(r,s,t\) be the roots of \(f\), counted with multiplicity. Since \(f\) is monic,
\[
f(x)=(x-r)(x-s)(x-t).
\]
Substituting \(x=0\) gives
\[
c=(-r)(-s)(-t)=-rst.
\]
In particular, \(c>0\) ensures that none of the roots is zero.

The monic polynomial with reciprocal roots is
\[
g(x)=\left(x-\frac1r\right)\left(x-\frac1s\right)\left(x-\frac1t\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
g(1)=\frac{(r-1)(s-1)(t-1)}{rst}.
\]
Changing the sign in each of the three numerator factors shows that
\[
(r-1)(s-1)(t-1)=-(1-r)(1-s)(1-t)=-f(1).
\]
Using \(rst=-c\) and \(f(1)=1+a+b+c\), we get
\[
g(1)=\frac{-f(1)}{-c}
=\boxed{\frac{1+a+b+c}{c}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
